title: reservations reserve: comma-separated multi-path batch in one call
action: Per exec-speed D4. In handleReservationsReserve (bee.mjs:1872): split the --path value on commas, trim, drop empties, dedupe. Single path => existing behavior byte-identical. Multiple paths => batch semantics inside ONE atomic section: with a topology, run findForeignHolds for ALL paths first — any foreign hold refuses the WHOLE batch listing every conflicting path (reserve nothing); then reserve() each path in order; if any individual reserve returns ok:false, release the reservations just made in this call (rollback via release()) and return ok:false with every conflict listed. All of this inside the SAME withHoldsLock section the single-path flow uses (reserve() never spawns children, so holding the lock across the loop is safe — same rationale as the existing comment). insertHold per successfully reserved path. Output: single path keeps today's shape; multi-path returns { ok, reservations: [...], conflicts: [...] } and a one-line text summary. Update command-registry.mjs reservations.reserve description + add a multi-path example. Do NOT touch lib/reservations.mjs.

semantic_judge.failure_signature: rollback releases only what this call granted — handleReservationsReserveBatch (.bee/bin/bee.mjs:2058) calls release(root, {agent, cell}), which reservations.mjs release() filters by agent+cell only, so a mid-batch conflict silently drops pre-existing reservations the same agent already held on that cell. Reproduced in an isolated scratch repo: agent A reserves p/one.txt (cell c1); agent B reserves p/three.txt (cell c2); A then runs `reserve --cell c1 --path "p/two.txt,p/three.txt"` — the batch correctly refuses, but `reservations list` afterwards shows A's p/one.txt gone (only B's row remains). A believes it still holds p/one.txt while the write guard no longer protects it.

checks.evidence: No release() or releaseHolds() call remains anywhere in handleReservationsReserveBatch (.bee/bin/bee.mjs:2038-2160); the only textual match is inside the BATCH_RACE_CONFLICT message explaining why no rollback is attempted. sessionsSeen / ledgerRollbackNeeded are gone.

checks.id: batch conflict semantics match reserve()'s own (isHardConflict)
checks.evidence: reserve() filters its findConflicts result through isHardConflict (reservations.mjs:543), so another agent's broad 'intent' row never refuses a fellow caller's exact-path reserve. The batch pre-check at bee.mjs:2067 calls findConflicts with NO isHardConflict filter, so an intent row hard-denies the whole batch. Reproduced live: planner reserves "src/api/*" --kind intent; worker's SINGLE reserve of src/api/a.ts returns ok:true, but worker's BATCH of "src/api/b.ts,src/api/c.ts" returns ok:false with the planner's intent row as the conflict. This is the exact 'hard deny from an intent record' that multisession-native-13 D4 and isHardConflict's own doc comment prohibit, and it makes a batch behave differently from N single reserves.

semantic_judge.failure_signature: batch conflict semantics match reserve()'s own (isHardConflict) — handleReservationsReserveBatch's new pre-check (.bee/bin/bee.mjs:2067) calls findConflicts(root, agent, paths) without reserve()'s isHardConflict filter, so another agent's broad 'intent' reservation hard-refuses the whole batch even though the identical single-path reserve succeeds. Reproduced: planner holds "src/api/*" --kind intent; worker single-reserves src/api/a.ts -> ok:true; worker batches "src/api/b.ts,src/api/c.ts" -> ok:false naming the intent row. Fix inside the declared files: filter the pre-check per requested path, e.g. dedupe over paths.flatMap((p) => findConflicts(root, agent, [p]).filter((c) => isHardConflict(c, p))) — isHardConflict is already exported by lib/reservations.mjs, so no change there is needed. The command-registry `kind` clause ("'intent' is advisory-only ... never hard-block") becomes true again once the filter is added.
